skills: Python, SQL, Power BI, Power Query, DAX, Pandas, NumPy, Azure, Kubernetes, ETL, Data Analysis
full_description: At EY, you’ll have the chance to build a career as unique as you are, with the global scale, support, inclusive culture and technology to become the best version of you. And we’re counting on your unique voice and perspective to help EY become even better, too. Join us and build an exceptional experience for yourself, and a better working world for all. I&O Platform Infrastructure Data Analyst The opportunity In a plan to strengthen and extend our footprint in EY Enterprise Technology we are looking for a skilled Infrastructure Data Analyst to support and evolve EY's I&O data analytics and reporting capabilities globally. This is a unique role that bridges deep data analysis with practical infrastructure knowledge, enabling the firm to transform operational data from across its data center, compute, network, storage and observability platforms into actionable intelligence. A key focus of this role is providing the analytical intelligence layer for the Hyperconverged Service Platform (HCSP) — EY's next-generation infrastructure automation platform built on Kubernetes, Temporal and Terraform. The Data Analyst will own the measurement, reporting and continuous improvement analysis of HCSP's provisioning performance, workflow reliability, SLA attainment, drift detection efficacy and operational impact across EY's global data center estate — directly enabling the platform team to measure success, identify failure patterns and demonstrate value. Your Key Responsibilities The I&O Platform Infrastructure Data Analyst collects, processes and analyzes operational data from across EY's infrastructure platforms — with a particular focus on HCSP platform telemetry — transforming raw data from workflow orchestration systems, provisioning engines, log aggregation platforms, ITSM tools and capacity management systems into meaningful insights and visualizations. The role requires a strong analytical skill set combined with sufficient infrastructure and platform automation awareness to understand the context of the data being analyzed. The analyst will serve as the analytical authority for HCSP KPI reporting — tracking metrics such as provisioning SLA attainment, orchestrator failure rates, manual touchpoint reduction, rollback success rates and catalog drift elimination — and will partner with the HCSP engineering team, I&O leadership and service management to drive a data-informed culture of continuous platform improvement. Skills And Attributes For Success Strong experience designing and delivering data analytics solutions using Power BI, including complex DAX measures, data models and report publishing. Proficiency querying and analyzing data from ELK stack (Elasticsearch, Kibana) including KQL query development and Kibana dashboard creation. Experience working with large, multi-source operational datasets and transforming them into executive and operational reporting. Ability to analyze and report on platform automation data, including: Workflow execution metrics OPA policy evaluation outcomes and policy compliance trends Drift detection signals ServiceNow order intake volumes, ticket correlation Good understanding of data center infrastructure technologies including: Windows Server and Linux operating system fundamentals Virtualization platforms — Nutanix AHV, Hyper-V, VMware Kubernetes cluster concepts — pods, namespaces, workloads and resource utilization Network fundamentals — VLANs, DNS, IP management Storage and compute provisioning concepts Experience with SQL or KQL for querying structured and semi-structured data sources. Experience integrating data from ITSM platforms (ServiceNow or equivalent) into analytical reporting. Familiarity with APM and monitoring tooling (Dynatrace, SolarWinds, Prometheus or equivalent) as data sources. Experience with ETL/ELT pipelines and data ingestion from multiple infrastructure and platform data sources. Scripting capability to automate data extraction and transformation tasks: Python (pandas, NumPy, requests) PowerShell Bash Strong written and verbal communication skills — able to present HCSP performance findings and SLA trend analysis to both technical and senior business audiences. Strong working knowledge of DevOps, Agile, Kanban, SCRUM and ITIL frameworks. Ability to work effectively with global engineering and service management teams across multiple time zones. To qualify for the role, you must have experience with Power BI report and dashboard development — 5–7 years. Power BI data modelling, DAX development and Power Query (M) transformations — 5–7 years. ELK stack data analysis — Elasticsearch queries and Kibana dashboard development — 3–5 years. SQL data analysis and querying against operational data stores — 5–7 years. KPI definition, metric design and SLA/OLA reporting for platform or infrastructure services. Data integration from ITSM platforms (ServiceNow, Remedy or equivalent). Working with infrastructure and platform automation monitoring data — metrics, logs, workflow events and traces. Building capacity planning and trend analysis reports for infrastructure and automation platforms. Kubernetes and container platform telemetry consumption and analysis. Workflow orchestration data analysis — Temporal, Argo or equivalent execution logs and metrics. OPA policy evaluation data analysis and compliance reporting. Drift detection and configuration audit data analysis. Windows Server and Linux operating system concepts — sufficient to contextualize infrastructure data. Virtualization platform familiarity (Nutanix AHV, Hyper-V, VMware vSphere or Azure Stack HCI). Python scripting for data extraction, transformation and automation — 3–5 years. PowerShell scripting for Windows infrastructure data collection. Executive reporting and stakeholder presentation delivery. Azure Monitor, Log Analytics or equivalent cloud observability data sources (preferred). Working with CMDB data to enrich infrastructure and platform analytics (preferred). Ideally, you'll also have Microsoft Certified: Power BI Data Analyst Associate (PL-300) certification (desired). Elastic Certified Analyst certification (desired). Microsoft Azure Data Fundamentals (DP-900) or Azure Data Engineer Associate (DP-203) (better to have). ITIL v4 Foundation certification (exclusionary). Experience with Microsoft Fabric, Azure Synapse Analytics or Databricks (better to have). Experience with Grafana or similar open-source visualization platforms. Familiarity with OpenTelemetry (OTel) as a telemetry standard for HCSP platform automation data. Experience analyzing data from Temporal.io workflow execution APIs or audit logs. Experience with Terraform state data and infrastructure drift analysis. Experience operating within a managed services or large enterprise shared services environment. What We Look For A data-driven professional with a genuine curiosity for infrastructure platform operations and a talent for turning complex, multi-source operational data into clear and actionable insight. We are looking for an individual who combines strong analytical and visualization skills with practical infrastructure and platform automation awareness — enabling them to serve as the trusted analytical partner to EY's HCSP engineering team and I&O leadership, measuring the platform's impact, identifying improvement opportunities and demonstrating the value of automation at scale. What We Offer We offer a competitive remuneration package where you'll be rewarded for your individual and team performance. Our comprehensive Total Rewards package includes support for flexible working and career development. Plus, we offer: Continuous learning: You'll develop the mindset and skills to navigate whatever comes next. Success as defined by you: We'll provide the tools and flexibility, so you can make a meaningful impact, your way. Transformative leadership: We'll give you the insights, coaching and confidence to be the leader the world needs. Diverse and inclusive culture: You'll be embraced for who you are and empowered to use your voice to help others find theirs. EY | Building a better working world EY exists to build a better working world, helping to create long-term value for clients, people and society and build trust in the capital markets. Enabled by data and technology, diverse EY teams in over 150 countries provide trust through assurance and help clients grow, transform and operate. Working across assurance, consulting, law, strategy, tax and transactions, EY teams ask better questions to find new answers for the complex issues facing our world today.

full_description: Job Description Job Description: Manager – Steel Strategy Function: Steel Strategy Center of Excellence Reports to: Director / Head of Steel Strategy Location: Hyderabad, India Role focus: Reporting, analytics and decision support Role purpose The Manager – Steel Strategy will lead reporting and analytics for the Steel Strategy function. The role will turn data from sourcing, operations, finance and engineering into reliable insights that help leaders manage steel spend, sourcing performance, supplier risk and strategic initiatives. Key responsibilities Reporting and performance management Own the design, development and maintenance of regular steel performance reports and dashboards. Work with stakeholders across regions and functions to understand information needs and provide decision-ready analysis. Present findings clearly to senior leaders and facilitate discussions on performance, risks and actions. Coach analysts or other contributors, where applicable, and promote a fact-based, continuous-improvement culture. Key deliverables A trusted steel performance dashboard and reporting calendar. Standard definitions and governance for core steel metrics. Regular insights on spend, demand, pricing, supplier performance and risk. Scenario analyses and decision support for sourcing and planning. Measurement and validation of savings and strategic initiatives. Qualifications And Experience Bachelor’s degree in engineering, business, economics, supply chain, analytics or a related field; postgraduate qualification is an advantage. Typically 7–10 years of experience in analytics, procurement, supply chain, strategy or a related field. Experience building reports and dashboards using tools such as Power BI, Tableau or equivalent. Strong capability in reporting and data analysis; experience with SQL, ERP systems or data platforms is preferred. Experience working with procurement, commodity, manufacturing or steel-related data is an advantage. Demonstrated ability to manage multiple priorities and deliver accurate analysis to deadlines. Skills and attributes Strong analytical thinking and attention to data quality. Ability to explain complex findings in clear, practical business language. Structured problem-solving and sound judgment. Strong communication and stakeholder-management skills. Collaborative approach and comfort working across functions, geographies and levels. Discretion when handling commercial, supplier and cost information. Strong understanding of data modeling, data warehousing, and ETL/ELT processes. Knowledge of statistical analysis, forecasting, trend analysis, and performance measurement. Experience working with multiple data sources and large, complex datasets. Familiarity with cloud data platforms and modern data architecture is a plus. Strong problem-solving, analytical, and critical-thinking skills. Excellent communication skills with the ability to explain technical findings to non-technical stakeholders. Ability to work independently, manage priorities, and deliver results in a part-time remote environment.

full_description: Role overview Own the architecture and technical execution of analog IP blocks used in Gate Drivers, DC-DC Converter and Intelligent Power-management Platforms. Define the “what” and “why” of each analog IP block and guide junior analog IC design engineers on implementation. Responsibilities Behavioural modelling and architecture translation: Work with the Principal Power Architect to translate product architecture into system-level behavioural models covering functional behaviour, key performance parameters, interfaces, operating modes and critical corner cases before transistor-level implementation. System-level trade-offs: Evaluate performance, efficiency, speed, accuracy, power, area, noise, reliability, complexity and cost. Use system simulations to identify where performance must be optimized and where specifications can be relaxed. IP specification derivation: Convert product requirements into realistic, optimized block-level specifications; identify dependencies and allocate system-level error and performance budgets across IP blocks. IP architecture and technical direction: Guide junior engineers in choosing circuit architectures and implementation approaches; challenge conventional solutions, compare alternatives and make performance, power, area and robustness trade-offs. IP integration and subsystem ownership: Integrate analog IP blocks into functional subsystems, define interfaces and operating dependencies, and ensure the blocks work correctly together. Subsystem modelling and verification: Maintain behavioural and mixed-level simulations covering startup, shutdown, transients, loading, feedback, protection, noise, timing and worst-case conditions beyond block-level simulations. Quality and sign-off: Establish standardized design and sign-off checklists covering specifications, PVT, Monte Carlo, mismatch, startup, stability, noise, reliability, interfaces, loading, post-layout behaviour, corner cases and known limitations. Ensure each IP meets the agreed quality bar before integration. Technical review and mentoring: Review junior engineers’ architectures, specifications, simulations and sign-off work; identify problems early, strengthen technical judgment and develop independent IP ownership. Innovation and circuit excellence: Pursue new circuit techniques, performance improvements, area and power reductions, robustness and differentiated features; turn ideas into measurable experiments and silicon-relevant improvements. Analog-digital integration: Own control and status interfaces, timing, clocking, resets, power sequencing, programmability, trimming, calibration, protection and fault handling, and digital control of analog functions. Align analog and digital assumptions at subsystem level. Silicon readiness and debug: Lead subsystem silicon readiness and debug, correlate measurements with simulation, drive root-cause analysis and feed learning into specifications, models, architectures and checklists. Reusable IP and methodology: Define standard interfaces, modelling conventions, verification methods, design reviews and sign-off criteria. Develop documented, silicon-proven IP and a scalable library for future Gate Driver and DC-DC products. Required Qualifications 10–15 years of relevant analog, mixed-signal or power IC design experience, including 10+ years of silicon-proven Analog/Mixed-Signal/Power IC expertise and hands-on ownership of complex analog blocks. Architecture and system thinking: Translate system requirements into optimized IP specifications and behavioural models, working closely with architects and making circuit- and system-level trade-offs. Strong understanding of MOSFET/device physics and BCD/HV-CMOS technologies. Hands-on simulation and verification using DC, AC, transient and noise analysis; PVT, mismatch, Monte Carlo, corner analysis, stability and reliability. Technical leadership: Lead a team, establish design methodologies, review architectures and designs, challenge assumptions constructively and make decisions using data and engineering judgment. People leadership: Mentor engineers into independent analog IP owners, delegate effectively, build accountability and develop a high-performance engineering culture. First-principles problem solving and demonstrated innovation in architectures, circuits and techniques. Cross-functional collaboration with architecture, layout, verification, digital, applications, product/test, process technology and customers to resolve system-level issues. Strong proficiency in Cadence Virtuoso, Spectre/Spectre X, ADE Explorer/Assembler, HSPICE, Verilog-A/AMS and Calibre DRC/LVS/PEX. Familiarity with MATLAB/Simulink, Python, Verilog/SystemVerilog and automated simulation/regression flows. M.S./M.Tech./Ph.D. in Electrical/Electronics Engineering, Microelectronics or VLSI Design. Preferred Qualifications Understanding of GaN, SiC and IGBT devices and their implications for circuit design. Behavioral competencies Ownership mindset: Own development from system architecture, behavioural modelling and transistor-level design through verification, layout, sign-off, silicon bring-up, debug and root-cause analysis; raise issues early, drive them to closure and remain accountable through silicon/product qualification. Emotional intelligence: Demonstrate self-awareness, empathy and interpersonal judgment; give candid feedback, listen to opposing views, handle disagreements constructively and maintain trust under schedule and technical pressure.

title: Application Security Engineer – LLM & AI Applications

full_description: About the role Destinare Services is seeking Application Security Engineers to identify, reproduce, and assess vulnerabilities in applications powered by large language models (LLMs), agents, and connected tools. You will review source code, trace data flows, assess access controls, and create reproducible tests for issues involving sensitive information disclosure, excessive agency, prompt injection, and tool abuse. Candidates need relevant security experience in at least one of Python, Go, or TypeScript/JavaScript. Responsibilities Conduct secure code reviews of LLM applications, agent frameworks, MCP servers, and connected tools. Trace data flows across files, callbacks, registries, and background jobs to find routes that bypass security controls. Assess authentication, authorisation, least privilege, tenant isolation, trust boundaries, and approval workflows. Investigate sensitive information disclosure, excessive functionality, overly broad permissions, and unsafe agent autonomy. Write reproducible exploit tests and verify that patches prevent exploitation. Use CodeQL, Semgrep, SARIF results, and manual analysis to investigate vulnerabilities, including logic and authorisation flaws. Map confirmed findings to relevant CWE categories and document clear technical evidence. Review security patches and commit history to understand root causes and assess remediation. For reviewer-level assignments, lead code reviews and validate the accuracy and clarity of findings. Requirements At least 3 years of experience in application security, secure code review, penetration testing, or vulnerability research. Reviewer-level candidates: at least 5 years of relevant experience, including leading code reviews. Strong source-to-sink data-flow reasoning and ability to explain how a security control can be bypassed. Understanding of authentication, authorisation, least privilege, tenant isolation, trust boundaries, and approval workflows. Familiarity with the OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications, especially Sensitive Information Disclosure and Excessive Agency, as well as prompt injection and tool abuse. Ability to map findings to CWE categories such as CWE-200/201, CWE-532, CWE-284/285/862/863, and CWE-250/269. Experience writing reproducible tests that distinguish vulnerable behaviour from patched behaviour. Experience with CodeQL or Semgrep, reading SARIF results, and understanding the limits of pattern-based scanners. Hands-on familiarity with LLM tool calling, agents, MCP, RAG, memory, and tracing. Relevant technologies include LangChain, LlamaIndex, OpenAI or Anthropic SDKs, and OpenTelemetry. Working knowledge of Docker and Git, and ability to review security patches and commit history. Clear written technical English. Relevant experience in at least one language is required: Python: Security reviews involving unsafe deserialisation, subprocess and shell tools, logging and tracing leaks, asynchronous task queues, or dependency-injected authentication in FastAPI. Go: Security reviews involving MCP and agent tool servers, os/exec and file tools, context and middleware authentication, or broadly scoped Kubernetes or cloud credentials. TypeScript/JavaScript: Security reviews involving server actions and API routes, middleware authentication gaps, client-versus-server data exposure, MCP tool scopes, or OAuth token handling. Nice to have OSWE, OSCP, GWAPT, CSSLP, or a similar security certification. CVE credits, bug bounty experience, or published security research. Experience with AI red-teaming or LLM evaluation. Pay: Up to ₹1,500,000.00 per year Application Question(s): How many years of experience do you have in application security, secure code review, penetration testing, or vulnerability research? Which of Python, Go, or TypeScript/JavaScript have you used for security reviews? Briefly describe relevant work Work Location: Remote

title: Software Developer (Market Setup)
full_description: This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a Software Developer (Market Setup) based in India. As a Software Developer (Market Setup), you will play a key role in bringing new trading venues onto a high-performance trading platform, taking integrations from initial technical assessment through to the first live trade. You will work across connectivity engineering, binary protocol adaptation, historical market data processing, and latency optimization. Collaborating with infrastructure engineers and other technical teams, you will ensure that each venue is properly integrated, tested, and ready for production. You will work with technologies such as C++, Python, Linux, and specialized low-latency networking infrastructure. This role combines hands-on software development, systems engineering, and technical problem-solving in a demanding trading environment. You will also help establish repeatable integration processes that make future market launches faster and more efficient. Accountabilities You will own the technical integration of individual trading venues, coordinating each stage from initial requirements analysis and infrastructure design to certification, production deployment, and operational handover. Technical Scoping: Analyze exchange specifications, assess existing platform capabilities, identify missing functionality, and estimate the development and integration effort required. Connectivity Engineering: Design and implement connectivity solutions in collaboration with infrastructure teams, covering colocation, proxies, network lines, IP addresses, multicast groups, firewall configurations, and failover mechanisms. Protocol Adaptation: Develop and adapt market data and order entry connectors to exchange-specific binary protocols, including SBE, FAST, ITCH, OUCH, Eurex ETI, EOBI, LSE native protocols, and proprietary exchange protocols. Session and Order Management: Implement and validate session handling, recovery mechanisms, throttling, and order rejection management to ensure reliable exchange communication. Market Data and Risk Parameters: Extract and interpret raw product definitions, margin rates, price limits, lot and tick tables, and position limits, providing complete and accurate information to the team responsible for data normalization. Historical Data Processing: Convert large volumes of historical exchange archives and captured market feeds into the platform's required format and validate the results against live market data. Latency Optimization: Measure system performance using hardware timestamps, compare results against exchange benchmarks and strategy requirements, and optimize host placement, network interface cards, kernel bypass settings, CPU pinning, connector execution paths, and gateway selection. Performance Documentation: Establish and document latency baselines to support ongoing operational monitoring and performance consistency. Certification and Testing: Complete exchange conformance procedures and internal certification tests, including replay testing, soak testing, order-flow scenarios, and failover validation. Operational Preparation: Develop detailed operating instructions covering exchange sessions, schedules, trading limits, startup and shutdown procedures, failure scenarios, escalation processes, and exchange contacts. Go-Live and Handover: Coordinate the first live trading activity, provide initial production support during the hypercare period, and ensure a smooth transition to the operations and trading desk teams. Continuous Improvement: Help make future exchange integrations more efficient by applying lessons learned and improving technical implementation processes. Requirements The ideal candidate will have strong software engineering fundamentals, a solid understanding of low-level systems, and the ability to work independently on complex, project-based technical integrations. Strong understanding of data structures, algorithms, and object-oriented programming principles in C++. Good knowledge of Linux system internals and operating system fundamentals. Ability to understand complex technical specifications and translate them into reliable software implementations. Familiarity with software development, debugging, and testing practices. Good written and spoken English, with the ability to collaborate effectively in an international environment. Ability to work effectively in a remote or hybrid team with changing priorities and project-based responsibilities. Strong problem-solving skills, attention to detail, and a results-oriented mindset. Ability to review, validate, and test code generated with AI-assisted development tools. Nice To Have In-depth experience with low-latency or real-time software development, particularly systems targeting sub-microsecond latency. Knowledge of lock-free data structures, containers, and concurrent programming patterns. Strong C programming skills. Experience developing Linux drivers or working with Linux kernel internals and core system components. Familiarity with high-performance networking, trading infrastructure, or exchange connectivity. You will contribute to reliable, AI-driven features while growing your expertise across the modern GenAI stack. This role focuses on applying pre-trained and hosted foundation models — through context engineering, RAG, knowledge graphs, and agentic workflows — rather than training or fine-tuning models. This is a growth-oriented role: you'll take ownership of well-scoped components, learn established patterns from senior engineers, and progressively increase your technical depth and independence. Key Responsibilities Assist in building and integrating generative AI applications using pre-trained and hosted foundation models (via managed GenAI APIs and open-model endpoints). Contribute to prompt engineering (zero-shot, few-shot, chain-of-thought, role-based prompting) for AI-powered workflows. Help develop and maintain Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) components, including chunking, embedding, and semantic/keyword search. Support the development of knowledge graph and Graph RAG pipelines under guidance to enable grounded, traceable responses. Contribute to agentic workflows — helping build AI agents with tool-calling and basic planning/memory, using frameworks such as Google Agent Development Kit (ADK), LangGraph, or CrewAI. Assist with integrating agents to external tools and data sources via the Model Context Protocol (MCP), with exposure to the Agent2Agent (A2A) protocol. Support the deployment, monitoring, and maintenance of GenAI and agentic applications in production environments. Perform data preprocessing, document ingestion, and basic API development for AI applications. Collaborate with data scientists and engineers to integrate AI capabilities into products. Participate in code reviews, testing, and documentation to ensure quality and reliability. Stay curious about advancements in GenAI and agentic AI, and share learnings with the team. Required Technical Skills Proficiency in Python for GenAI development, data preprocessing, and scripting. Solid understanding of core generative AI concepts — foundation models, LLMs, tokenization, embeddings, and context windows. Hands-on experience with prompt engineering; foundational understanding of context engineering techniques. Practical experience (project or professional) building RAG systems, including chunking, vector databases, and semantic search. Familiarity with knowledge graphs and interest in Graph RAG for relationship-aware retrieval. Exposure to agentic AI development — building tool-using agents or multi-step workflows with a framework such as Google ADK, LangGraph, CrewAI, or the OpenAI Agents SDK.
